title.narrative: Collect More ¿ Spend Better: Domestic Revenue Mobilisation with the International Tax Compact

description.narrative:
Enhancing fiscal space represents a key prerequisite for mobilising the funds needed to implement the Sustainable Development Goal (SDGs) and a green, digital, just and resilient COVID-19 pandemic recovery. This is all the more pertinent in contexts of low- and middle-income countries, where fiscal space was often narrow or non-existent even before the global pandemic. Domestic revenues are the most important and sustainable source to create this fiscal space and finance activities to achieve the SDGs by 2030.

Therefore, the overall objective of this Action is to increase the availability of domestic resources for financing sustainable development. This is achieved via support to the Addis Tax Initiative (ATI), an established multi-stakeholder partnership that aims to promote fair and effective domestic revenue mobilisation (DRM) in low- and middle-income countries, policy coherence and the social contract through partnerships and knowledge building. Committing to the ATI fosters partner countries¿ efforts to establish tax systems that work for people and achieve the SDGs. Further support to the Network of Tax Organisations (NTO) aims at the same objective via strengthening tax organisations through capacity development, internal collaboration and peer-learning as well as participating in the global tax dialogue.

This Multi-Donor Action is jointly co-financed by the European Union (EU) and the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and implemented by Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) as part of the BMZ project `Sector Programme Good Financial Governance (SP GFG)¿ (PN 19.2032.1).
